extracted.intended_audience: UC Berkeley staff, researchers, departmental communicators, and requesters of media-relations support
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting, approving, and distributing UC Berkeley press releases, covering structure, content, timeline, and distribution practices for university news items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press Release Structure and Style
rubrics_metrics.description: UC Berkeley press releases are usually a few pages in length, written as a news story, include quotes from the source(s) and give context to the news being reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the release as a journalistic news story (not promotional), include relevant quotes, and provide background/context so reporters can understand the significance. Substantive stories may span multiple pages; avoid one-line announcements that lack context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate communication tool (press release vs media advisory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication Tools Available: Press release — written as a news story with quotes and context; Media advisory — quickly lists the 'who, what, where and when'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a press release for substantive announcements that require narrative, quotes and context. Use a media advisory when you need to quickly notify media of the basic logistical facts (event invites, times, locations) without a full story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline: allow about two weeks' notice
rubrics_metrics.description: UC Berkeley Media Relations needs about two weeks' notice to issue a press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide at least two weeks so Media Relations can gather information, conduct interviews, write the release, obtain necessary approvals, and decide which reporters to alert. Shorter lead times reduce ability to coordinate and craft a full story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press Release Boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: A standardized brief paragraph describing UC Berkeley, providing journalists essential context about the university, used at the end of every press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the approved UC Berkeley boilerplate at the end of each release to give reporters concise institutional context. Do not substitute informal or ad-hoc descriptions of the university.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-release-worthy: significant research breakthroughs
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant research breakthroughs are considered press-release-worthy by Berkeley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the research constitutes a clear, newsworthy advance before requesting a release; Media Relations will coordinate with researchers and consider embargo timing for journal-linked publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-release-worthy: academic achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic achievements (e.g., notable appointments, distinctions) are considered grounds for a press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide documentation of the achievement and context that explains its importance beyond the academic unit to help Media Relations craft a broader-angle news story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-release-worthy: campus programs of broad interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Campus programs that have broad interest across audiences are considered suitable for press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the program's reach and why it matters to broader communities; Media Relations will help frame the story for external audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-release-worthy: major awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Major awards received by faculty, students, or the university are considered press-release-worthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the award’s prestige, selection criteria, and relevance; include quotes and contextual details to help reporters understand significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-release-worthy: newsworthy events
rubrics_metrics.description: Events that are newsworthy (by impact, novelty, or public interest) qualify for press release consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details about the event’s news angle, participants, outcomes, and why it merits external coverage; Media Relations will decide whether a full release or a media advisory is more appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing approach: write as a news story (not promotional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should be written as news stories rather than promotional materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on facts, context, and journalistic tone; avoid marketing language or overtly promotional phrasing. Use clear lede, supporting facts, and quotes that advance the news narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing approach: include quotes from sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should include quotes from the source(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide meaningful, attributable quotes that add perspective, explain significance, or humanize the story. Work with Media Relations to craft or refine quotes as needed for clarity and journalistic use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing approach: provide context
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should provide context to the news being reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply background information, implications of the news, and any necessary technical explanation so reporters can place the announcement in broader perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing approach: allow multiple pages for substantive stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive stories may require multiple pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an announcement involves complex research or multiple facets, be prepared to provide longer narrative support, supporting materials, and possibly supplemental factsheets or links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing approach: tone should be journalistic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt neutral, objective, news-reporting tone suitable for journalists rather than promotional communications. Prioritize clarity, accuracy, and readability for general audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution: strategic targeting of relevant reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution should include strategic targeting of relevant reporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify reporters and outlets most likely to cover the topic; Media Relations will coordinate targeted outreach rather than broad, untargeted blasts to maximize pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution: coordinate with researchers and departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution should be coordinated with researchers/department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work collaboratively with the affected researchers and department units to secure approvals, quotes, and timing; alignment helps ensure accurate messaging and readiness for media inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution: use of embargo when tied to journal publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases are often paired with embargo if tied to journal publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a release relates to a journal article, Media Relations may request an embargo to coordinate simultaneous release with the journal; follow embargo rules and timelines to maintain relationships with journalists and publishers.
